son in law, and thy sons, and thy daughters, and whatsoever thou hast in the city, bring <hi type="italic">them</hi> out of this place:<div eID="gen2356" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen2357" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">12. </hi>Et dixerunt viri ad Lot, Adhuc est aliquis tibi hic? generum, et filios tuos, et filias tuas, et omnia, quae sunt tibi in civitate, educ de loco:<div eID="gen2357" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen2358" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">13. </hi>For we will destroy this place, because the cry of them is waxen great before the face of the LORD; and the LORD hath sent us to destroy it.<div eID="gen2358" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen2359" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">13. </hi>Quia disperdimus nos locum hunc, eo quod crevit clamor eorum coram Jehova: et misit nos Jehova ad perdendum eum.<div eID="gen2359" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen2360" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">14. </hi>And Lot went out, and spake unto his sons in law, which married his daughters, and said, Up, get you out of this place; for the LORD will destroy this city. But he seemed as one that mocked unto his sons in law.<div eID="gen2360" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen2361" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">14. </hi>Et egressus est Lot, et loquutus est ad generos suos, qui acceperant filias ejus, et dixit, Surgite, egredimini de loco isto, quia disperdit Jehova civitatem: et fuit sicut ludens in oculis generorum suorum.<div eID="gen2361" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen2362" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">15. </hi>And when the morning arose, then the angels hastened Lot, saying, Arise, take thy wife, and thy two daughters, which are here; lest thou be consumed in the iniquity of the city.<div eID="gen2362" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen2363" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">15. </hi>Quum vero aurora ascendisset, instabant angeli ipsi Lot, dicendo, Surge, cape uxorem tuam, et duas filias tuas, quae adsunt, ne forte pereas in punitione civitatis.<div eID="gen2363" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen2364" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">16. </hi>And while he lingered, the men laid hold upon his hand, and upon the hand of his wife, and upon the hand of his two daughters; the LORD being merciful unto him: and they brought him forth, and set him without the city.<div eID="gen2364" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen2365" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">16. </hi>Et tardabat: et apprehenderunt viri manum ejus, et manum uxoris ejus, et manum duarum filiarum ejus, eo quod parceret Jehova ei: et eduxerunt eum, et posuerunt eum extra urbem.<div eID="gen2365" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen2366" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">17. </hi>And it came to pass, when they had brought them forth abroad, that he said, Escape for thy life; look not behind thee, neither stay thou in all the plain; escape to the mountain, lest thou be consumed.<div eID="gen2366" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen2367" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">17. </hi>Et fuit, quum eduxissent ipsi eos foras, dixit, Evade pro anima tua, ne respicias post to, nec stes in tota planitie: in monte serva to, ne forte pereas.<div eID="gen2367" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen2368" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">18. </hi>And Lot said unto them, Oh, not so, my Lord:<div eID="gen2368" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen2369" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">18. </hi>Et dixit Lot ad eos, Ne quaeso domini mei:<div eID="gen2369" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen2370" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">19. </hi>Behold now, thy servant hath found grace in thy sight, and thou hast magnified thy mercy, which thou hast shewed unto me in saving my life; and I cannot escape to the mountain, lest some evil take me, and I die:<div eID="gen2370" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen2371" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">19. </hi>Ecce, nuncinvenit servus tuus gratiam in oculis tuis, et magnificasti misericordiam tuam, quam fecisti mecum, ut vivificares animam meam: et ego non potero servare me in monte, ne forte haereat mihi malum, et moriar:<div eID="gen2371" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen2372" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">20. </hi> Behold now, this city <hi type="italic">is</hi> near to flee unto, and it <hi type="italic">is</hi> a little one: Oh, let me escape thither, ( <hi type="italic">is</hi> it not a little one?) and my soul shall live.<div eID="gen2372" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen2373" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">20. </hi>Ecce, nunc civitas ista propinqua, ut fugiam illuc, et est parva: evadam nunc illuc: numquid non parva est, et vivet anima mea?<div eID="gen2373" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen2374" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">21. </hi>And he said unto him, See, I have accepted thee concerning this thing also, that I will not overthrow this city, for the which thou hast spoken.<div eID="gen2374" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen2375" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">21. </hi>Et dixit ad eum, Ecce, suscepi faciem tuam etiam in hoc, ut non suvbertam civitatem, ut loquutus es.<div eID="gen2375" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen2376" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">22. </hi>Haste thee, escape thither; for I cannot do any thing till thou be come thither. Therefore the name of the city was called Zoar.<div eID="gen2376" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen2377" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">22. </hi>Festina, serva to illuc: quia non potero facere quicquam, donec ingrediaris illuc: idcirco vocavit nomen civitatis Sohar.<div eID="gen2377" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen2378" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">23. </hi>The sun was risen upon the earth when Lot entered into Zoar.<div eID="gen2378" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen2379" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">23. </hi>Sol egressus est super terram, et Lot ingressus est Sohar.<div eID="gen2379" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen2380" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">24. </hi>Then the LORD rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from the LORD out of heaven;<div eID="gen2380" type="x-p"/> </cell><cell> <div sID="gen2381" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">24. </hi>Et Jehova pluit super Sedom et super Hamorah sulphur et ignem a Jehova e coelis.<div eID="gen2381" type="x-p"/> </cell> </row><row> <cell> <div sID="gen2382" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">25. </hi>And he overthrew those cities, and all the plain, and all the inhabitants of                   <ns0:p n="1">1 AND the LORD appeared unto him, in the plains of Mamre, and he sate in the tent door <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Waiting for strangers which might pass that way, for whom no publick places being provided in those times and places, vertuous persons used to entertain them in their houses.                   <ns0:p n="7">7 And Abraham ran unto the herd and fetcht a calf, tender and good, and gave <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> unto a young man, and he hasted to dress it.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="8">8 And he took butter, and milk, and the calf <ns0:note n="*" place="bottom">To wit, the choicest parts of the calf.</ns0:note> which he had dressed, and set <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> before them, and he stood by them <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">To wait upon them, as the word <ns0:hi>standing</ns0:hi> is used, <ns0:hi>Nehem.</ns0:hi> 12. 44. <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 52. 12.</ns0:note> under the tree, and they did eat <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Either seemingly, as the Scripture oft speaks of things ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cording to appearance; or really, they received the meat into the bodies which they assumed, where it was consumed by a Divine power.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>

                  <ns0:p n="10">10 And he said, I will certainly return unto thee <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Not in a visible shape, but with my powerful and effectual presence, to fulfill my promise.</ns0:note>

Or, 2. to the Child, <ns0:hi>ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cording to the time of Life, i. e.</ns0:hi> in the time which is usual for the Conception, Quickning, and Bringing forth of a living Child.                   <ns0:p n="12">12 Therefore Sarah laughed <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">Not from joy and admiration, but from distrust and con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tempt, as if it were incredible.</ns0:note> within herself <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">Heb. <ns0:hi>In her heart, i. e.</ns0:hi> she secretly derided it, though none but her self, as she thought, knew it.</ns0:note>, saying, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luk. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">

                  <ns0:p n="13">13. And the LORD said unto Abraham, Where<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore did Sarah laugh, saying, shall I of a surety bear a Child which am old?</ns0:p>

                  <ns0:p n="19">19 For I know him <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">I know him to be such an one as I am now descri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bing: Or, I know this concerning him which now follows.
